findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests, not jobs/mailers
findings.body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale), never the fallback locales returned by I18n.fallbacks. Fallback locales are loaded solely by ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, so code running outside a request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console) in a non-English locale will attempt fallback lookups against locale files that were never loaded and return 'translation missing' instead of the site-default/English string, unless a web request previously happened to load them in the same process. The fix must load the fallback chain inside the translation path (or ensure_loaded! must be invoked for all execution contexts), not just in a controller before_filter.

findings.title: Fallback calculation crashes if default_locale is unset and depends on DB-backed settings during translation
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every fallback lookup. If default_locale is nil/blank (fresh install, boot/rake/migration contexts before site settings are available, or a cleared setting), this raises NoMethodError on nil (or produces the invalid locale :""), turning an otherwise recoverable missing-translation case into an exception for any I18n.t call. It also makes the low-level I18n backend depend on a database-backed SiteSetting lookup during translation, including during initialization when the settings table may not exist yet. Guard nil/blank and avoid requiring SiteSetting availability for the :en fallback.

findings.title: Fallback list recomputes SiteSetting lookup on every missing translation
findings.body: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks invokes I18n.fallbacks[locale] each time it retries a lookup, and this implementation allocates a new array and calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym (a settings-store lookup) on every invocation, with no memoization. On pages/emails with many untranslated keys in a non-English locale this adds repeated settings lookups and allocations to the hot translation path, partially defeating the translation LRU-cache accelerator. Cache the computed chain per locale (invalidating when default_locale changes) or compute the default once.

findings.title: No tests cover the new fallback chain or its interaction with lazy locale loading
findings.body: This PR replaces Rails' config.i18n.fallbacks with a custom FallbackLocaleList, changes the backend module inclusion (pluralization + fallbacks), deletes the old pluralization initializer, and adds a lazy ensure_loaded! path, but adds no specs. There is no coverage proving: a missing key in a user locale falls back to the site locale then :en, fallback files are actually loaded on demand, pluralization still works through the fallback locale, or behavior outside ApplicationController. Given the lazy-loading accelerator makes fallback success dependent on which locales happen to be loaded, a regression would silently surface as 'translation missing' strings in production.
